title: How the Amityville Horror Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the Amityville Horror story, beginning with the November 13, 1974 murders of six members of the DeFeo family at 112 Ocean Avenue in Amityville, New York, by Ronald "Butch" DeFeo Jr. They cover the Lutz family's move into the house, the alleged paranormal events (priest Father Ralph Pecoraro's blessing, flies, pig-like beast, cold room, door and windows blown out), their flight after about 28 days (neighbors say ten days), and the book by Jay Anson (1977), the 1979 film, and media appearances including WPIX and In Search Of. The hosts then poke holes in the story: lawyer William Weber's later claim it was a hoax concocted over wine, conflicting accounts, lawsuits, the house's 2017 sale for about $600,000, and the lack of later supernatural reports. The episode ends with a listener mail segment about a homeless man who saved a dog, and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Amityville introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about fall, Josh's new website, and introduce the Amityville Horror as the episode topic.

segments.title: The house and its look
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Dutch colonial house at 112 Ocean Avenue, its eye-like windows, its address change, and its current appearance.

segments.title: The DeFeo family murders
segments.summary: On November 13, 1974, Ronald DeFeo Jr. killed six family members with a rifle. He first blamed the mafia, later claimed voices told him to kill, and was sentenced to six consecutive life terms.

segments.title: The Lutz family buys the house
segments.summary: About a year after the murders, George and Kathy Lutz and their three children bought the house for about $80,000, despite being told of the murders.

segments.title: Priest blessing and early haunting claims
segments.summary: Father Ralph Pecoraro blessed the house and reported a cold room, a voice saying get out, and car malfunctions. The family reported flies, a red-eyed pig-like beast, and 3:15 a.m. waking.

segments.title: Alleged legends and the final night
segments.summary: George Lutz researched the house and learned of Shinnecock land and legends, including Hans Holzer's grave theory. The family fled after a stormy night in which the door and windows blew out.

segments.title: Book deal and publicity
segments.summary: The Lutzes left the house and contacted Jay Anson, whose 1977 book The Amityville Horror became a bestseller and made the family celebrities.

segments.title: William Weber and the business dispute
segments.summary: Attorney William Weber first brought the story to the public at a press conference, but was cut out of the book deal. The Lutzes and DeFeo's cut were disputed.

segments.title: Media appearances and the WPIX photo
segments.summary: The Lutzes appeared on talk shows, and Channel 5 WPIX staked out the house. A black-and-white photo was debuted by George Lutz; the hosts debate whether it shows a boy. The Warrens appeared on In Search Of, where Father Pecoraro was shown with his face hidden.

segments.title: The 1979 film and its legacy
segments.summary: The 1979 film starring James Brolin and Margot Kidder was a box-office hit; it was shot in Tom's River, New Jersey, since Amityville denied filming permits. The hosts discuss its cultural impact and the 2005 remake.

segments.title: Holes in the story: timeline and house condition
segments.summary: The hosts note the conflicting departure timelines (28 days vs. 10 days) and that the house's hinges and windows were shown intact by later owner Barbara Camardi, while the newspaper photo was of a screen door.

segments.title: Hoax claims, lawsuits, and Father Pecoraro's credibility
segments.summary: George Lutz maintained the story until his death in 2006. William Weber later claimed the story was a hoax made over wine. Many lawsuits followed. The priest's account was questioned, and the house sold in 2017 for about $600,000 below asking.

segments.title: Skepticism: no later reports and placebo effect
segments.summary: The hosts discuss that no later owners reported supernatural events, Lorraine Warren's explanation, the Lutzes not contacting police, and whether a violent history changes a home's energy, concluding placebo effect and expectation may explain experiences.

segments.title: Pointer to HowStuffWorks article
segments.summary: Josh mentions a HowStuffWorks article on the Amityville Horror by Matt Hunt.

segments.title: Listener mail: homeless man saves dog
segments.summary: Ali from New Hampshire writes that a homeless man on a bicycle blocked traffic to save her dog Sophia, who was running into the street. The hosts follow up on a homelessness episode rerun.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh gives listener contact information and the show signs off.
